intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that vitelliform macular dystrophy-4 (VMD4) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the IMPG1 gene (602870) on chromosome 6q14.

checks.claim: Vitelliform macular dystrophy-4 (VMD4) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the IMPG1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that IMPG1 mutations cause both autosomal-dominant and -recessive forms of VMD
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant families carry the p.Leu238Arg mutation; heterozygosity follows from dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: Vitelliform macular dystrophy-4 (VMD4) is caused by homozygous mutation in the IMPG1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Two individuals from one family affected by autosomal-recessive VMD were homozygous for the splice-site mutation c.807+1G>T
checks.explanation: Homozygous mutation reported in recessive family.

checks.claim: The IMPG1 gene is located on chromosome 6q14.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in IMPG1 cause vitelliform macular dystrophies.
checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature not stated in abstract; accepted per instructions.

paragraphs.text: Vitelliform macular dystrophy is a retinal disorder. Its hallmark is yellowish, egg-yolk-like (vitelliform) deposits of subretinal material in the macula. These deposits can lead to progressive loss of central vision. VMD4 is a form of adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy caused by mutation in IMPG1, a gene that encodes a component of the interphotoreceptor matrix. It can show autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Vitelliform macular dystrophy is a retinal disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Vitelliform macular dystrophies (VMD) are inherited retinal dystrophies
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The hallmark of vitelliform macular dystrophy is yellowish, egg-yolk-like (vitelliform) deposits of subretinal material in the macula.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by yellow, round deposits visible upon fundus examination
checks.explanation: Abstract mentions yellow round deposits but not egg-yolk-like, subretinal, or macular location explicitly.

checks.claim: The vitelliform macular deposits in vitelliform macular dystrophy can lead to progressive loss of central vision.
checks.evidence_quote: All individuals were symptomatic, reported a slowly progressing central vision loss over years and did not receive any specific ocular treatment.
checks.explanation: Progressive central vision loss is described.

checks.claim: VMD4 is a form of adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy caused by mutation in IMPG1.
checks.evidence_quote: These genes should be screened in adult-onset vitelliform dystrophy with (1) moderate visual impairment
checks.explanation: IMPG1 is identified as a causal gene in a late-onset or adult-onset vitelliform dystrophy.

checks.claim: IMPG1 encodes a component of the interphotoreceptor matrix.
checks.evidence_quote: IMPG1 encodes the SPACR protein, a component of the rod and cone photoreceptor extracellular matrix domains.
checks.explanation: Interphotoreceptor matrix component; the conclusion also refers to the interphotoreceptor matrix.

checks.claim: VMD4 can show autosomal dominant inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: IMPG1 mutations cause both autosomal-dominant and -recessive forms of VMD
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: VMD4 can show autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: IMPG1 mutations cause both autosomal-dominant and -recessive forms of VMD
checks.explanation: Stated.

paragraphs.text: Manes et al. (2013) reported both autosomal dominant and autosomal recessive transmission of VMD4. In the dominant families, affected individuals carried heterozygous IMPG1 mutations. In the recessive family, the affected individuals carried a homozygous IMPG1 mutation.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) reported autosomal dominant transmission of VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: subsequently found in two other families with autosomal-dominant VMD and the same phenotype
checks.explanation: Dominant families reported.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) reported autosomal recessive transmission of VMD4.
checks.evidence_quote: Two individuals from one family affected by autosomal-recessive VMD were homozygous for the splice-site mutation c.807+1G>T
checks.explanation: Recessive families reported.

checks.claim: In the autosomal dominant VMD4 families reported by Manes et al. (2013), affected individuals carried heterozygous IMPG1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: identification of a c.713T>G (p.Leu238Arg) IMPG1 mutation, which was subsequently found in two other families with autosomal-dominant VMD
checks.explanation: All three dominant families had the same single mutation (not plural mutations), and the abstract does not explicitly say they were heterozygous; this is only implied by dominant inheritance.

checks.claim: In the autosomal recessive VMD4 family reported by Manes et al. (2013), affected individuals carried a homozygous IMPG1 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: Two individuals from one family affected by autosomal-recessive VMD were homozygous for the splice-site mutation c.807+1G>T, and two from another family were compound heterozygous
checks.explanation: There were two recessive families; one was homozygous and the other compound heterozygous. The claim implies a single recessive family.

paragraphs.text: Vitelliform macular dystrophy is genetically heterogeneous. Another form, VMD5, is caused by mutation in the IMPG2 gene, which encodes the related interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2. Other forms of vitelliform macular dystrophy are caused by mutation in the BEST1 and PRPH2 genes.

checks.claim: Vitelliform macular dystrophy is genetically heterogeneous.
checks.evidence_quote: IMPG1 and IMPG2 are new causal genes in 8% of families negative for BEST1 and PRPH2 mutations.
checks.explanation: Several causal genes are named for the disorder.

checks.claim: Vitelliform macular dystrophy-5 (VMD5) is caused by mutation in the IMPG2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: IMPG1 was the causal gene in 3 families (IMPG1 1-3, 11 patients) and IMPG2 in a fourth family (2 patients).
checks.explanation: IMPG2 is identified as a causal gene. The VMD5 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: IMPG2 encodes interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycan-2, a protein related to IMPG1.
checks.evidence_quote: The interphotoreceptor matrix proteoglycans-1 and -2, also known as sialoprotein associated with cones and rods (SPACR) and SPACRCAN (a proteoglyCan related to SPACR), respectively
checks.explanation: IMPG2 (SPACRCAN) is described as related to IMPG1 (SPACR).

checks.claim: Some forms of vitelliform macular dystrophy are caused by mutation in the BEST1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: many BMD and some AVMD cases harbor mutations in BEST1 or PRPH2
checks.explanation: Stated.

checks.claim: Some forms of vitelliform macular dystrophy are caused by mutation in the PRPH2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: many BMD and some AVMD cases harbor mutations in BEST1 or PRPH2
checks.explanation: Stated.

paragraphs.text: Manes et al. (2013) studied families with vitelliform macular dystrophy. They identified heterozygous mutations in the IMPG1 gene in families with autosomal dominant disease and a homozygous IMPG1 mutation in a family with autosomal recessive disease.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) studied families with vitelliform macular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large family with autosomal-dominant VMD, gene mapping and whole-exome sequencing led to the identification
checks.explanation: Families with VMD were studied.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) identified heterozygous IMPG1 mutations in families with autosomal dominant vitelliform macular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: identification of a c.713T>G (p.Leu238Arg) IMPG1 mutation, which was subsequently found in two other families with autosomal-dominant VMD
checks.explanation: A single mutation, not plural mutations, was found in all dominant families; heterozygosity is implied rather than stated.

checks.claim: Manes et al. (2013) identified a homozygous IMPG1 mutation in a family with autosomal recessive vitelliform macular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: Two individuals from one family affected by autosomal-recessive VMD were homozygous for the splice-site mutation c.807+1G>T
checks.explanation: Stated. The abstract also reports a compound heterozygous recessive family, which the draft omits.

paragraphs.text: Meunier et al. (2014) also identified IMPG1 mutations in patients with adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy.

checks.claim: Meunier et al. (2014) identified IMPG1 mutations in patients with adult-onset vitelliform macular dystrophy.
checks.evidence_quote: IMPG1 was the causal gene in 3 families (IMPG1 1-3, 11 patients)
checks.explanation: IMPG1 mutations were found in patients with late-onset or adult-onset vitelliform dystrophy.
